doc_screened_files.reason: Best match for the `F-late-resolution-error-recovery` / `F-skip-resolution-after-duplicate-param` labels: duplicated generic-parameter names are diagnosed here, and the bug likely comes from still recording a usable resolution for the invalid `M` binding.

The query stack goes through `AstConv::create_substs_for_ast_path` and `instantiate_mono_trait_ref` immediately before the ICE, so this is where the malformed trait substitutions are built from the resolved path.
This is the exact panic site (`const_param_out_of_range`) where the malformed substitution finally trips the invariant, so it is a strong downstream symptom even if not the original cause.
The failing query is `impl_trait_ref` during `collect_mod_item_types`, and this file owns that collection path for lowering the impl’s trait reference before later substitution happens.
This module validates and converts generic argument lists, including const-generic defaults, so duplicate `M` parameters can poison the argument mapping that later becomes the bad substitution.
Generic parameter definitions and instantiation live here; an off-by-one or duplicate-name handling bug would explain how `M/#2` ends up referenced as an out-of-range const parameter.
This pass assigns definitions to generic parameters before late resolution finishes, so incorrect recovery around duplicate params here could leave later stages with malformed generic metadata.
This crate root wires the collection and type-checking pipeline together, so it is a plausible integration point where invalid duplicate-parameter recovery can leak into later substitution work.
The reproducer uses a const parameter with a default (`const M: u8 = M`), so const-generic value handling here is a secondary suspect for how the malformed const default is represented.

General item/body checking sits downstream of collection and can amplify bad generic-state recovery, making it a weaker but still relevant place to inspect for propagation of the malformed trait item.
